title: AI Risk Management Framework
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. AI RMF 1.0 released 26 January 2023 for voluntary use; four functions Govern, Map, Measure, Manage; Generative AI Profile (NIST-AI-600-1) released 26 July 2024; AI RMF 1.0 being revised as part of the White House AI Action Plan; critical infrastructure profile concept note 7 April 2026.

title: AI RMF 1.0: characteristics of trustworthy AI
publisher: NIST Trustworthy and Responsible AI Resource Center
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Seven characteristics of trustworthy AI; accuracy measured with false positive and false negative rates on realistic test sets, possibly by segment; three bias categories (systemic, computational and statistical, human-cognitive) that can occur without intent; trade-offs between characteristics are context value choices.

title: AI Act: regulatory framework for AI
publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
supports: Opened with WebFetch; page updated 19 October 2026. In force 1 Aug 2024; bans and AI literacy 2 Feb 2025; generally applicable 2 Aug 2026; AI Omnibus in force 27 Jul 2026 moving high-risk rules to 2 Dec 2027 (Annex III) and 2 Aug 2028 (Annex I); four risk levels; high-risk examples (credit scoring, recruitment, education) and obligations.

title: AI literacy - Questions & Answers
publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
supports: Opened with WebFetch; updated 20 October 2026. Article 4 applies to providers and deployers from 2 Feb 2025, supervised and enforced by national authorities from 2 Aug 2026; no specific level mandated; no certificate required; internal records suffice.

title: Introduction to AI assurance
publisher: GOV.UK, Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 12 February 2024 by DSIT; explains how AI assurance techniques support safe and responsible development and deployment, within the wider AI governance landscape.

title: Portfolio of AI assurance techniques
publisher: GOV.UK, Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 7 June 2023; case studies mapped to the white paper principles; techniques: impact assessment, impact evaluation, bias audit, compliance audit, certification, conformity assessment, performance testing, formal verification.

title: FTC Announces Crackdown on Deceptive AI Claims and Schemes
publisher: Federal Trade Commission
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 25 September 2024, Operation AI Comply, five actions; DoNotPay had not tested its output against a human lawyer's and agreed to pay $193,000; chair's statement that there is no AI exemption from existing law.

title: 29 CFR 1607.4 - Information on impact
publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (copy of the eCFR text)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (eCFR redirected to a bot check, which was not bypassed; this is a copy of the regulation text). Four-fifths rule: a selection rate below 80% of the highest group's is generally regarded as evidence of adverse impact; smaller differences may count if significant; larger may not with small numbers.

title: Automated Employment Decision Tools (AEDT)
publisher: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Local Law 144 of 2021: no AEDT use without a bias audit within one year before use, public audit information and notices to candidates; enforcement began 5 July 2023.

title: Classification: Accuracy, recall, precision, and related metrics
publisher: Google for Developers, Machine Learning Crash Course
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Definitions of accuracy, recall, false positive rate and precision; accuracy misleading on imbalanced data (99% example at 1% positives); which metric to prefer by error cost; threshold trade-off.

title: Metrics and scoring: quantifying the quality of predictions
publisher: scikit-learn 1.9.1 documentation
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Choose a strictly consistent scoring function; balanced accuracy; precision and recall formulas; ROC AUC; average precision baseline equals the share of positives; dummy estimators as baselines.

title: Probability calibration
publisher: scikit-learn 1.9.1 documentation
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Definition of calibration; calibration curves; Brier score mixes calibration and discrimination; sigmoid vs isotonic, isotonic as good or better with about 1,000 or more samples; typical calibration of logistic regression, naive Bayes, random forests and SVMs.

title: Cross-validation: evaluating estimator performance
publisher: scikit-learn 1.9.1 documentation
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Hold out a test set; k-fold; stratified folds and the note that stratification can understate fold variance; GroupKFold for grouped samples; TimeSeriesSplit for time-ordered data; shuffling harms non-i.i.d. data.

title: Common pitfalls and recommended practices
publisher: scikit-learn 1.9.1 documentation
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Data leakage definition; split first, fit on training only, use pipelines; leaky feature selection gives 0.76 test accuracy on random data where 0.5 is correct; controlling randomness with random_state.

title: Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in ML-based Science
publisher: Sayash Kapoor and Arvind Narayanan, Princeton University
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Patterns, 2023; leakage errors found in 41 papers across 30 fields, affecting 648 papers; leakage types; model info sheets proposal.

title: Rules of Machine Learning: Best Practices for ML Engineering
publisher: Google for Developers (Martin Zinkevich)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Rule 1, do not be afraid to launch without machine learning; Rule 2, design and implement metrics first; Rule 3, move from complex heuristics to ML; training-serving skew rules.

title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems
publisher: NeurIPS Proceedings (D. Sculley et al., NIPS 2015)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. ML systems incur ongoing maintenance costs; risk factors include boundary erosion, entanglement, hidden feedback loops, undeclared consumers, data dependencies, configuration issues and changes in the external world.

title: Stop Explaining Black Box Machine Learning Models for High Stakes Decisions and Use Interpretable Models Instead
publisher: arXiv (Cynthia Rudin; Nature Machine Intelligence, 2019)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Argues for inherently interpretable models instead of post-hoc explanations of black boxes in high-stakes decisions.

title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
publisher: arXiv (Margaret Mitchell et al.; FAT* 2019)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Short documents accompanying trained models, stating intended use and benchmarked performance across groups and conditions, and how evaluation was done.

title: Datasheets for Datasets
publisher: arXiv (Timnit Gebru et al.; Communications of the ACM, 2021)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Proposes that every dataset ship with a datasheet recording its motivation, composition, collection process and recommended uses.

title: Inherent Trade-Offs in the Fair Determination of Risk Scores
publisher: arXiv (Jon Kleinberg, Sendhil Mullainathan, Manish Raghavan; ITCS 2017)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Three fairness conditions for risk scores cannot all be satisfied simultaneously except in highly constrained special cases.

title: Common fairness metrics
publisher: Fairlearn documentation (0.16 development version)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Demographic parity difference and ratio; equalized odds; cautions that passing a metric does not make a system fair, small subgroups are unreliable, multiple comparisons raise false findings, and against applying the four-fifths rule in most cases.

title: How Not To Run an A/B Test
publisher: Evan Miller (author's site)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 18 April 2010. Peeking and stopping at the first 5% significance reading gave a 26.1% false positive rate in his simulation; fix sample size in advance, or use sequential or Bayesian designs; rule of thumb n = 16 sigma^2 / delta^2 with sigma^2 = p(1 - p).

title: Diagnosing Sample Ratio Mismatch in Online Controlled Experiments: A Taxonomy and Rules of Thumb for Practitioners
publisher: Microsoft Research (Aleksander Fabijan et al., KDD 2019)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Defines sample ratio mismatch as an observed split different from the expected one, a symptom of data quality issues; ignoring it can make a bad change look good or the reverse.

title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, 7.3.3 Comparisons based on data from two processes
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Two-proportion z-test with pooled proportion for reasonably large samples; Fisher's exact test for small samples.

title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, 7.2.4.2 Sample sizes required
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Sample size formulas for testing a proportion from alpha, beta and the change to detect; Fleiss, Levin and Paik continuity correction; worked example of about 102, or 112 with correction.

title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, 7.1.4 What are confidence intervals?
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Confidence intervals and their link to hypothesis tests; meaning of a 95% interval under repeated sampling; wider intervals when sigma is estimated.

title: Misuse of p-values
publisher: Wikipedia (encyclopedia summary)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Encyclopedia summary citing Wasserstein and Lazar (2016), The American Statistician 70(2): a p-value is not the probability the null is true or that results arose by chance alone; 0.05 is a convention; p-values do not measure effect size. Used because the ASA PDF and journal page could not be read.

title: Causal Inference: What If
publisher: Miguel A. Hernán and James M. Robins (author's site)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Chapman & Hall/CRC, 2020; free to download; causal inference without models, with models, and from longitudinal data.

title: Statistics overview
publisher: GrowthBook documentation
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Bayesian engine by default and a frequentist engine with sequential testing and CUPED; sample ratio mismatch check; multiple testing corrections in the frequentist engine; open source under MIT.
